name: Today's Report
headline: Insurance costs are showing up in home prices, most of all near downtown.
teaser: Mortgage rates eased a touch. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year at 7.17% this morning, down 0.02, and the 15-year unchanged at 6.83%. The 10-Year, which mortgage rates follow, closed Monday at 4.96%.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Mortgage rates eased a touch. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year at 7.17% this morning, down 0.02, and the 15-year unchanged at 6.83%. The 10-Year, which mortgage rates follow, closed Monday at 4.96%.

Today's housing story is insurance. A new Brookings working paper by USC economists Matthew Kahn and Wesley Miller finds that homeowners insurance strain is highest near downtown, where natural hazard risk is lowest. Using Treasury data for 2018 through 2022, ZIP codes within a mile of downtown paid average premiums 39% higher than ZIP codes more than five miles out, and insurers declined to renew about 20% more often.

It shows up in prices. In the paper, a one standard deviation rise in insurance strain went with single family prices about 10.6% lower, and 19.1% lower right downtown, fading to near zero by 30 miles out. The authors call it an association, not proof of cause, and they did not break out the Bay Area. Nobody tours a house for the insurance quote, but every buyer pays it.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Board wide: 2,727 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 194 coming soon and 202 brand new.
  • Five city ledger: 705 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 621 are already on the market and 84 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 252 live, 201 active, 37 coming soon, 14 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,199,999 at $782 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 32 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 184, Milpitas 111, Newark 92, Union City 66.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,090,000 at $675 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 172 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: the ledger slipped to 705 from 717, and homes sitting 60 days or longer rose again, to 172 from 167 yesterday and 161 the day before. Buyers: get a homeowners insurance quote in the first days of escrow, before contingencies come off, because it belongs in the monthly payment math. Sellers: have your roof age, permits and any claims history ready, since a quick, clean insurance quote keeps a buyer moving.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Oil fell for a fourth straight session Monday, and it is holding near $100.47 this morning. The 10-Year is edging up, near 4.97%, after Monday's 4.96% close.

Gold and silver each gave back about 1% on Monday and are a little lower again this morning, gold near $4,364 and silver near $66.20. Market Briefs printed gold and Brent as higher on Monday; both fell, and the cards use the exchange prints.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Monday belonged to tech. The Nasdaq jumped 2.26% as Meta rose 11.34% after its new AI app, Muse, overtook ChatGPT as the top free iPhone app in the U.S. Sensor Tower counts more than 2.5 million downloads since its September 8 launch.

AMD rose 9.95% and closed above $1 trillion in market value for the first time, joining Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron (chart above). Four years ago no U.S. chipmaker was worth that much; now four are. AMD is up about 187% this year.

images.alt: Ranked bar chart of the market value of U.S. chipmakers worth $1 trillion or more at the September 21, 2026 close: Nvidia $5.48 trillion, Broadcom $1.73 trillion, Micron $1.18 trillion and AMD $1.00 trillion, with Intel shown as the next largest at $0.61 trillion.
images.caption: AMD closed above $1 trillion in market value for the first time on Monday, the fourth U.S. chipmaker to get there. Intel, the next largest, is worth about $0.61 trillion.
images.source: Source: Nasdaq closing prices, September 21, 2026, times shares outstanding from each company's latest SEC filing.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html:
Bitcoin's six-day climb is the story (chart above). It closed Monday at $86,505, its highest close since January 28 and up 14.3% from last week's low of $75,650. Most of that came in two days, about 6% Friday and 6.5% Monday, and it is about 35% above where it was three months ago.

Market Briefs printed Bitcoin at $81,177, Ethereum at $2,639 and XRP at $1.41, the same three numbers it printed on Monday. Ours are live from CoinGecko as of 9:11 AM PT: Bitcoin is holding near $86,218, and XRP is the day's big mover, up 4.40% over 24 hours.

images.alt: Line chart of Bitcoin's daily closing price from September 15 to September 21, 2026: $75,650 on September 15, near $76,000 through Thursday, $80,944 on Friday, near $81,000 over the weekend and $86,505 on Monday, below a dashed line at $89,178 marking January 28, the last time Bitcoin closed higher. A dashed leg shows Tuesday morning's live price near $86,400.
images.caption: Bitcoin closed Monday at $86,505, up 14.3% from last week's low and its highest close since January 28. The dashed leg is Tuesday morning's live price, not a close.
images.source: Source: Coin Metrics reference rate, daily close at 00:00 UTC; Tuesday's live price from CoinGecko.
